candidates.title: A Phase 1/2, Open-label, Multicenter, Dose Escalation and Cohort Expansion Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Anti-CD70 Allogeneic CRISPR-Cas9-Engineered T Cells (CTX131) in Adult Subjects With Relapsed or Refractory Solid Tumors
candidates.abstract: This is an open-label, multicenter, Phase 1/2 study evaluating the safety and efficacy of CTX131™ in subjects with relapsed or refractory solid tumors. An open-label, multi-center Phase 1/2 study of CTX131 in subjects with relapsed/refractory solid tumors. CTX131 is an is allogeneic CD70- directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell immunotherapy comprised of allogeneic T cells that are genetically modified ex vivo using CRISPR-Cas9 (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/ CRISPR associated protein 9) gene editing components (single guide RNA and Cas9 nuclease). Status: COMPLETED. Phase: PHASE1. Sponsor: CRISPR Therapeutics AG.
candidates.title_ja: 再発または難治性固形腫瘍を持つ成人被験者における抗CD70異種CRISPR-Cas9遺伝子組みそT細胞(CTX131)の安全性と有効性に関する第1/2相オープンラベル多施設投与投与量増強およびコホート拡大研究
candidates.abstract_ja: これは、再発または難治性固形腫瘍患者におけるCTX131™の安全性と有効性を評価するオープンラベル多施設第1/2相試験です。再発・難治性固形腫瘍患者を対象としたCTX131のオープンラベル多施設第1/2相試験です。CTX131は、異体遺伝子CD70指向キメラ抗原受容体(CAR)T細胞免疫療法であり、CRISPR-Cas9(クラスター状の規則的に間隔された短い回文リピート/CRISPR関連タンパク質9)遺伝子編集成分(シングルガイドRNAおよびCas9ヌクレアーゼ)を用いて、異体変異体T細胞を体外で遺伝子改変しています。状態:完了。フェーズ:フェーズ1。スポンサー:CRISPR Therapeutics AG。

candidates.title: A Multi-center, Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo-controlled, Parallel-group Trial to Assess the Efficacy of Daridorexant on Nighttime Symptoms and Daytime Functioning in Adult and Elderly Participants With Insomnia Disorder
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this clinical trial is to collect more data about the effect of daridorexant in adults and elderly people with insomnia disorder. The trial aims to find out whether daridorexant can help improve: * how trial participants sleep at night, * how trial participants function the next day. Researchers will compare daridorexant to a placebo (a look-alike inactive substance that contains no active medicine) to understand which effect daridorexant has on total sleep time and next-day functioning. Enrolled participants will: * Take daridorexant 50 mg or placebo once daily for approximately 3 months * Visit the clinic once every month during treatment for checkups and tests * Keep a sleep diary of the number of hours they sleep and how well they sleep * Complete a questionnaire every day about any symptoms of sleepiness during the day and any impact on physical and mental functioning such as energy levels, mood, or ability to concentrate or memorize. The trial includes three trial periods: Following a Screening period, during which it will be checked if participants are eligible to take part, eligible participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either daridorexant 50 mg or placebo for ca. 3 months (Treatment period). On completion of treatment, participants will be followed for up to 10 days for safety assessments (Safety follow-up period). Trial participation will end with a Follow-up call (Participant Last Visit) at the end of the Safety follow-up period. The maximum trial duration for an individual participant will be approximately 4 months. Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd..
candidates.title_ja: 成人および高齢者の不眠症患者における夜間症状および日中の機能に対するダリドレキサントの有効性を評価するための多施設、二重盲検、ランダム化プラセボ対照群並行群試験
candidates.abstract_ja: この臨床試験の目的は、成人および不眠症高齢者におけるダリドレキサントの効果についてさらに多くのデータを収集することです。この試験は、ダリドレキサントが以下の改善に役立つかどうかを調べることを目指しています:* 試験参加者の夜間の睡眠状況、* 試験参加者の翌日の機能改善。研究者は、ダリドレキサントとプラセボ(有効薬を含まない類似の不活性物質)を比較し、ダリドレキサントが総睡眠時間や翌日の機能にどのような影響を与えるかを把握します。登録参加者は以下を行います:* ダリドレキサント50mgまたはプラセボを約3か月間1日1回服用 * 治療中は月に一度クリニックで健康診断や検査を受ける * 睡眠時間と睡眠の質を記録した睡眠日記をつける * 日中の眠気の症状やエネルギーレベル、気分、集中力や記憶力などの身体的・精神的機能への影響について毎日アンケートを記入します。試験は3つの試験期間で構成されています。スクリーニング期間中は参加者の参加資格が確認され、対象者は1:1の比率で約3か月間ダリドレキサント50mgまたはプラセボのいずれかを投与されます(治療期間)。治療終了後、参加者は最大10日間の安全性評価(安全性追跡期間)の追跡期間が行われます。試験参加は安全性追跡期間終了時にフォローアップコール(参加者最終訪問)で終了します。個々の参加者の最大試験期間は約4か月となります。ステータス:NOT_YET_RECRUITING。フェーズ:フェーズ3。スポンサー:Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd.

candidates.title: MAGNITUDE-2: A Phase 3, Multinational, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of NTLA-2001 in Participants With Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN)
candidates.abstract: This study will be conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a single dose of nexiguran ziclumeran (NTLA-2001) compared to placebo in participants with ATTRv-PN. This is a multinational, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in approximately 60 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive a single infusion of either nexiguran ziclumeran or placebo. To ensure all participants will have the potential to receive nexiguran ziclumeran, participants will have the option to cross over to the opposite study arm at Month 12 or Month 18, depending on study criteria. Status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Intellia Therapeutics.
candidates.title_ja: MAGNITUDE-2:遺伝性トランスティレチンアミロイドーシスおよび多発性神経障害(ATTRv-PN)患者におけるNTLA-2001の有効性と安全性を評価するための第3相多国籍無作為化二重盲検プラセボ対照試験
candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究は、ATTRv-PNの参加者を対象に、単回投与のネキシグラン・ジクルメラン(NTLA-2001)の有効性と安全性をプラセボと比較して評価することを目的としています。これは約60名の参加者を対象とした多国籍・多施設・二重盲検・プラセボ対照試験で、参加者は1対1で無作為に割り当てられ、ネキシグラン・ジクルメランまたはプラセボのいずれかを単回の点滴を受けます。すべての参加者がネキシグラン・ジクルメランを受けられる可能性を確保するため、参加者は研究基準に応じて12か月目または18か月目に反対の研究群に移行する選択肢があります。ステータス:ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING。フェーズ:フェーズ3。スポンサー:インテリア・セラピューティクス。

candidates.title: RNA Vaccination Drives Expansion and Brain-Licensing of T Cells to Enhance the Efficacy of Adoptive Cell Therapy in Glioblastoma.
candidates.abstract: Adoptive cell therapies using chimeric antigen receptor or T cell receptor-transgenic T cells (TCR-T) are effective in treating hematological malignancies but have limited efficacy in solid tumors, particularly brain tumors. A major challenge of adoptive T cell therapy in brain tumors is lack of access to the target antigen, which is necessary for restimulation and persistence. Here, we addressed this challenge by using an mRNA vaccine encoding the cognate antigen to induce in vivo restimulation of transferred TCR-T cells in glioma models. Delivery of mRNA encoding the immunodominant MHC class I ovalbumin epitope SIINFEKL to splenic dendritic cells initiated strong expansion of adoptively transferred ovalbumin-specific OT1 CD8+ T cells to up to 80% of all circulating CD8+ T cells. RNA vaccination markedly improved T cell infiltration and retained interferon-stimulated gene signature in the brain, suppressing glioblastoma growth. The therapeutic efficacy of this approach was further demonstrated in an experimental model for a first-in-class TCR-T cell therapy targeting an HLA-A2-restricted immunodominant epitope of the human glioblastoma stemness antigen PTPRZ1. Co-administration of human dendritic cells transfected with PTPRZ1-mRNA led to rejection of orthotopically implanted primary human gliomas endogenously expressing PTPRZ1 and HLA-A2 after adoptive transfer of PTPRZ1-TCR-T cells. In summary, these findings indicate that mRNA vaccines can boost TCR-T cell therapy against glioblastoma.
candidates.title_ja: RNAワクチン接種はT細胞の増殖と脳ライセンス付与を促進し、膠芽腫における採用細胞療法の有効性を高めます。
candidates.abstract_ja: キメラ抗原受容体またはT細胞受容体-トランスジェニックT細胞(TCR-T)を用いたアダプティブ細胞療法は、血液悪性腫瘍の治療に効果的ですが、特に脳腫瘍などの固形腫瘍では効果が限定的です。脳腫瘍におけるアダプティブT細胞療法の大きな課題は、再刺激と持続に必要な標的抗原へのアクセス不足です。本研究では、関連する抗原をコードするmRNAワクチンを用いて、膠質腫モデルにおける移管されたTCR-T細胞の生体内再刺激を誘導することでこの課題に取り組みました。免疫優位のMHCクラスIオベルブミンエピトープSIINFEKLをコードするmRNAを脾臓樹状細胞に送達すると、養子移植されたオブアルブミン特異的OT1 CD8+ T細胞が循環中のCD8+ T細胞の最大80%に強く増殖しました。RNAワクチン接種はT細胞浸潤を著しく改善し、脳内のインターフェロン刺激遺伝子シグネチャーを保持して膠芽腫の増殖を抑制しました。このアプローチの治療効果は、ヒト膠芽腫幹抗原PTPRZ1のHLA-A2制限免疫優性エピトープを標的とした初の実験モデルでさらに実証されました。PTPRZ1-mRNAをトランスフェクトしたヒト樹状細胞の共同投与により、PTPRZ1-TCR-T細胞の導入後にPTPRZ1およびHLA-A2を内因性に発現する直来植床原発ヒトグリオーマの拒絶反応が見られました。まとめると、これらの知見はmRNAワクチンが膠芽腫に対するTCR-T細胞療法を強化することを示しています。

candidates.title: In Silico Evaluation of the Effects of Temperature on the Affinity of the SV2C Ligand UCB-1A to SV2 Paralogs.
candidates.abstract: Synaptic vesicle glycoproteins 2 (SV2) are integral membrane proteins essential for neurotransmitter release and are implicated in neurological disorders including epilepsy and Parkinson's disease. In the attempt to develop a ligand selective for SV2C, and i in collaboration with UCB Biopharma, UCB-F was identified as a potential candidate. However, the affinity of UCB-F to SV2C was found to be temperature dependent, decreasing by about 10-fold from 4 to 37 °C. UCB-1A was subsequently identified as SV2C ligand displaying in vitro a 100-fold selectivity for SV2C compared with SV2A. In this study, we investigated whether the binding of UCB-1A to SV2A and SV2C was affected by the temperature. A combination of experimental binding assay data and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used. The binding studies revealed that UCB-1A affinity for SV2A decreased significantly at 37 °C compared with 4 °C, whereas binding to SV2C remained largely unchanged. MD simulations reproduced these observations, namely that ligand RMSD values at 37 °C showed that UCB-1A binding fluctuated markedly in the SV2A complex, with many trajectories exceeding the 3.0 Å stability cutoff, whereas UCB-1A remained relatively well-anchored in SV2C under the same conditions. Structural analysis showed that, while UCB-1A adopts a conserved binding pose across all paralogs stabilized by π-π stacking and a hydrogen bond with Asp, SV2C possesses a unique stabilizing feature. In SV2C, Tyr298 is less exposed to the solvent and engages in a persistent hydrogen bond with Asparagine, a structural feature that reinforces pocket stability and limits temperature-induced destabilization. This interaction is absent in SV2A, consistent with its greater temperature sensitivity. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic explanation for the experimentally observed temperature independence of UCB-1A binding to SV2C. More broadly, the results highlight the importance of incorporating physiologically relevant temperatures into SV2 ligand evaluation and demonstrate how combining experiments with simulations can uncover isoform-specific mechanisms of ligand recognition and stability.
candidates.title_ja: シリコにおけるSV2C配位体UCB-1AのSV2パラログへの親和性に対する温度の評価。
candidates.abstract_ja: シナプス小胞糖タンパク質2(SV2)は神経伝達物質の放出に不可欠な膜タンパク質であり、てんかんやパーキンソン病などの神経疾患に関与しています。SV2Cに対する選択的リガンドの開発を試み、UCBバイオファーマと共同でUCB-Fが候補として特定されました。しかし、UCB-FのSV2Cへの親和性は温度依存的であり、4°Cから37°Cへ約10倍に低下しました。UCB-1Aは後にSV2Cリガンドとして同定され、SV2Cに対してSV2Cに対してin vitroでSV2Aと比べて100倍の選択性を示します。本研究では、UCB-1AのSV2AおよびSV2Cへの結合が温度によって影響を受けるかどうかを調査しました。実験結合アッセイデータと分子動力学(MD)シミュレーションを組み合わせて使用しました。結合研究により、UCB-1AのSV2A親和性は37°Cで4°Cに比べて有意に低下し、SV2Cへの結合はほぼ変化がなかったことが明らかになりました。MDシミュレーションではこれらの観察が再現され、37°CでのリガンドRMSD値はSV2A複合体内でUCB-1A結合が著しく変動し、多くの軌道が3.0Åの安定性カットオフを超えたことが示されました。一方、UCB-1Aは同じ条件下でもSV2Cに比較的よく固定されていました。構造解析の結果、UCB-1Aはすべての対序物で保存された結合ポーズを採り、π-πスタッキングとAspとの水素結合によって安定化していますが、SV2Cは独自の安定化特徴を持つことが示されました。SV2Cでは、Tyr298は溶媒への曝露が少なく、アスパラギンと持続的な水素結合を形成します。これはポケット安定性を強化し、温度による不安定化を抑制する構造的特徴です。この相互作用はSV2Aには存在せず、SV2Aの温度感度が高いことと一致しています。これらの発見は、UCB-1AがSV2Cに結合する実験的に温度非依存性が観察されているメカニズムを説明しています。より広くは、生理学的に関連性の高い温度をSV2リガンド評価に組み込む重要性を浮き彫りにし、実験とシミュレーションを組み合わせることで、リガンド認識と安定性のアイソフォーム特異的メカニズムを明らかにできることを示しています。

candidates.title: A Phase 1, Non-randomized, Open-label, Multi-center Study to Assess the Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Intravenous Fosmanogepix in Adult Subjects With End-stage Renal Disease Requiring Intermittent Hemodialysis
candidates.abstract: This study will evaluate how fosmanogepix is processed by the body (pharmacokinetics, PK) in participants with kidney failure (end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring intermittent hemodialysis (IHD) compared with participants with normal kidney function (control group). Fosmanogepix is given by intravenous infusion and is converted in the body to manogepix, the active form of the drug. Fosmanogepix is an investigational and has not been approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or any other regulatory authority for use in humans. The study will also evaluate the effect of hemodialysis on manogepix levels in participants with ESRD. The safety and tolerability of fosmanogepix will also be assessed in participants with kidney failure and in matched participants with normal kidney function. Participation in the study will last up to 11 weeks and will include up to two study periods. Participants with ESDR requiring IHD will receive fosmanogepix in two study periods. Healthy participants will receive fosmanogepix in one study period. The study will be conducted at two study sites in the United States. Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE1. Sponsor: Basilea Pharmaceutica.

candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究では、間欠性血液透析(IHD)を必要とする末期腎疾患(ESRD)患者と正常な腎機能を持つ患者(対照群)におけるフォスマノゲピックスの体内処理(薬剤動態学、PK)を評価します。フォスマノゲピックスは静脈内点滴で投与され、体内で有効薬剤であるマノゲピックスに変換されます。フォスマノゲピックスは臨床試験薬であり、米国食品医薬品局(FDA)やその他の規制当局によってヒト使用の承認を受けていません。また、ESRD患者における血液透析がマノゲピックスレベルに与える影響も評価します。フォスマノゲピックスの安全性および忍容性は、腎不全の参加者および正常な腎機能を持つ適合した参加者に対しても評価されます。研究への参加期間は最大11週間で、最大2つの研究期間が含まれます。IHDを必要とするESDRの参加者は、2つの研究期間にわたりフォスマノゲピックスを投与されます。健康な参加者は1つの研究期間でフォスマノゲピックスを投与されます。本研究は米国内の2か所で実施されます。状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ1。スポンサー:Basilea Pharmaceutica。

candidates.title: Emerging GPCR Agonist-Based Therapies to Trigger the Resolution of Inflammation.
candidates.abstract: The long-lasting paradigm that inflammation resolves through a passive decline of pro-inflammatory signals has been fundamentally revised by extensive research demonstrating that the resolution of inflammation is an active, programmed, and tightly regulated process driven by a temporally coordinated sequence of molecular and cellular events for restoring tissue homeostasis. Under physiological conditions, specialized lipid pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), as well as some pro-resolving proteins and peptides, initiate the resolution of inflammation process by halting pro-inflammatory immune cell recruitment, clearance of effector cells and cellular inflammatory debris, tissue repair, and restoration of local immunity. Clinical and experimental observations indicate that failure to activate this endogenous pro-resolving program or alteration of SPM synthesis leads to persistent inflammatory activity, contributing to chronic diseases such as arthritis, Alzheimer's disease, cancer, and inflammatory bowel disorders through excessive neutrophil infiltration, impaired efferocytosis, and unresolved tissue damage. Advances in the understanding of SPMs, their biology, and their mechanisms have driven the development of new therapeutic molecules mimicking the activity of endogenous pro-resolving lipids or pro-resolutive proteins and derivatives. Multiple classes of molecules, including stabilized lipid analogs, peptides, and agonist antibodies, have shown promising preclinical activity, particularly through ChemR23 (gene CMKLR1) and formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) targeting. Ongoing and completed phase I/II clinical trials report encouraging results in conditions such as eczema and ocular diseases, with favorable safety profiles. Unlike traditional anti-inflammatory strategies, these approaches engage a natural physiological program rather than inhibiting or depleting inflammatory pathways, aiming to establish long-term tissue homeostasis without compromising the immune system. Emerging pro-resolutive G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) therapies are designed for enhanced target specificity, biodistribution, and specific pro-resolutive signaling for sustained efficacy. Targeting pro-resolving GPCRs holds strong potential to redefine the treatment of inflammatory diseases by promoting the active reinstatement of immune balance and homeostasis.
candidates.title_ja: 炎症の解消を促進するための新たなGPCR作動薬ベースの治療法。
candidates.abstract_ja: 炎症が炎症促進シグナルの受動的な減少によって解決するという長期的なパラダイムは、炎症の解決が組織恒常性を回復するための分子および細胞イベントの時間的に調整された一連の過程によって駆動される、能動的でプログラム的かつ厳密に制御されたプロセスであることを実証した広範な研究によって根本的に修正されました。生理学的条件下では、特殊な脂質促進解消媒介剤(SPMs)や一部の促進解消タンパク質やペプチドが、炎症促進免疫細胞の動員停止、エフェクター細胞や細胞炎症残骸の除去、組織修復、局所免疫の回復を通じて炎症の解決を開始します。臨床および実験的観察は、この内因性解決促進プログラムやSPM合成の変化が活性化されない場合、持続的な炎症活性を引き起こし、関節炎、アルツハイマー病、がん、炎症性腸疾患などの慢性疾患に寄与し、過剰な好中球浸潤、悪化したエフェロサイトーシス、未解決の組織損傷によるものであることを示しています。SPMsの理解、その生物学的およびそのメカニズムの進展により、内因性解消脂質や解消促進タンパク質および誘導体の活性を模倣する新しい治療分子の開発が促進されています。安定化脂質類似体、ペプチド、作動剤抗体など複数の分子クラスが、特にChemR23(遺伝子CMKLR1)およびホルミルペプチド受容体2(FPR2)の標的化を通じて有望な前臨床活性を示しています。進行中および完了した第I/II相臨床試験は、湿疹や眼疾患などの疾患において有望な結果を報告しており、安全性も良好です。従来の抗炎症戦略とは異なり、これらのアプローチは炎症経路を抑制または枯渇させるのではなく、自然な生理学的プログラムを用い、免疫系を損なうことなく長期的な組織恒常性の確立を目指しています。新興の解疑促進型Gタンパク質結合受容体(GPCR)療法は、標的特異性の向上、生体分布、特異的解消性シグナル伝達を目的に設計されており、持続的な有効性を保っています。解決促進型GPCRを標的化することは、免疫バランスと恒常性の能動的回復を促進することで炎症性疾患の治療を再定義する大きな可能性を秘めています。

candidates.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Phase III Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HMPL-306 in Participants With Postoperative Residual or Recurrent Grade 2 Glioma Harboring IDH1 or IDH2 Mutations
candidates.abstract: This study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of HMPL-306 in participants with postoperative residual or recurrent grade 2 gliomas carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations. This study plans to enroll approximately 210 participants with postoperative residual or recurrent grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations who have previously received only surgical treatment. Participants meeting all enrollment eligibility criteria will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive HMPL-306 250 mg or placebo matched to HMPL-306 administered orally once daily (QD). Participants will continue to receive study drug treatment in 28-day cycles until BIRC-confirmed PD, death, occurrence of intolerable toxicity, et al, whichever occurs first. Participants in the placebo group with BIRC-confirmed PD, after evaluation, may cross over to the HMPL-306 group to receive HMPL-306 treatment. Status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Hutchmed.
fields: Grade 2 Astrocytoma or Oligodendroglioma With an IDH1 or IDH2 Mutation

candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究は、IDH1またはIDH2変異を持つ術後残存または再発性グレード2神経腫を持つ参加者におけるHMPL-306の有効性と安全性を評価する、ランダム化、二重盲検、プラセボ対照、多施設第III相臨床試験です。本研究は、術後残存または再発性のグレード2アストロサイトーマまたは少突起膠腫を持ち、これまでに手術治療のみを受けたことがある約210名の参加者を登録する予定です。すべての登録適格基準を満たす参加者は、HMPL-306 250mgまたは経口投与1日1回(QD)と一致したプラセボを1:1の比率で無作為化されます。参加者は、BIRCによって確定されたPD、死亡、耐受不能な毒性の発生などのいずれか早い方まで、28日周期で研究用薬治療を継続します。IRCで確定されたPDのプラセボ群の参加者は評価後、HMPL-306群に移行してHMPL-306治療を受けることができます。ステータス:NOT_YET_RECRUITING。フェーズ:フェーズ3。スポンサー:Hutchmed。

candidates.title: A Multicenter, Open-label, Single-arm, Baseline-controlled Trial to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Lucerastat in Treatment-naïve/Pseudo-naïve Adult Male Participants With Fabry Disease
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this clinical trial is to learn how well lucerastat works and how safe it is in untreated adult male participants with Fabry disease. The main question this clinical trial aims to answer is: • Does treatment with lucerastat affects the amount of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3), a fatty substance that builds up in the kidneys, in untreated adult men with Fabry disease? This is an open-label, single-arm trial, which means that participants will know which trial medication they receive and only one trial medication will be given. Trial participants will: * Take lucerastat every day for 18 months * Have kidney biopsies at the end and start of the trial * Visit the clinic 10 times for check-up and tests * Take part in the trial for up to 21 months in total Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd..

candidates.title: A Randomized, Open-Label, Phase 3 Trial of Epcoritamab vs Investigator's Choice Chemotherapy in Relapsed/Refractory Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (R/R DLBCL)
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this trial is to find out if epcoritamab, also known as EPKINLY™ and GEN3013, is safe and works well as treatment for participants with DLBCL that are not responding to treatment, have grown in size, or have come back following treatment with at least 1 prior systemic cancer therapy. All participants in this trial will be randomly assigned to receive either epcoritamab or a pre-specified investigator's choice (standard of care) chemotherapy (either rituximab + gemcitabine + oxaliplatin \[R-GemOx\], or bendamustine + rituximab \[BR\]). Participants must have failed or be ineligible to receive an autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT). Epcoritamab will be injected under the skin. Investigator's choice chemotherapy will be given intravenously. Trial details include: * The trial duration will be up to 5 years after last participant is randomized. * All trial participants have a 21-day screening period, a treatment period, and a follow-up period that continues until death. * The estimated trial duration for an individual participant depends upon the treatment arm assigned: * Participants who receive epcoritamab will have 28-day treatment cycles. Epcoritamab will be given once weekly for the first 3 months, then every other week for 6 months, then every 28 days until lymphoma progression or unacceptable adverse events. * Participants who receive investigator's choice (standard of care) chemotherapy will receive treatments either: * R-GemOx: On Day 1 (or Day 1 \& Day 2), and Day 15 (or Day 15 \& Day 16) every 28 days, for up to 4 months; or * BR: On Day 1 and Day 2 every 3 weeks for up to 4.5 months. The trial is an open label, multi-center, global phase-3 randomized trial of epcoritamab. The goal of this randomized trial is to evaluate the efficacy of epcoritamab (GEN3013, DuoBody®-CD3xCD20) compared to investigator's choice of chemotherapy, in participants with relapsed, refractory DLBCL who have failed or are ineligible for high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplant (HDT-ASCT). No change in chemotherapy is permitted for participants during the treatment phase of the trial. Overall Survival (OS) is the primary endpoint in USA and in China, with the analysis population including all randomized participants. OS/Progression Free Survival (PFS) are dual-primary endpoints for rest of the world (outside US and China), with the analysis population also including all participants randomized. The China sub-study of GCT3013-05 is registered under NCT07226752. Status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Results: Posted. Sponsor: Genmab.
candidates.title_ja: 再発/難治性びまん性大B細胞リンパ腫(R/R DLBLCL)におけるエコリタマブとInvestigator's Choice化学療法のランダム化オープンラベル第3相試験
candidates.abstract_ja: 本試験の目的は、EPKINLYおよびGEN3013とも呼ばれるEPKINLY™およびが、治療に反応しない、体格が大きくなっている、または少なくとも1回の全身がん治療後に再発したDLBCLの参加者に対して安全かつ治療として有効かどうかを明らかにすることです。本試験の全参加者は、エコリタマブまたは事前に指定された研究者の選択(標準治療)化学療法(リツキシマブ+ジェムシタビン+オキサプラチン/[R-GemOx]、またはベンダムスチン+リツキシマブ\[BR\]のいずれか)を受けます。参加者は自己幹細胞移植(ASCT)を受けに失敗しているか、不適格でなければなりません。エコリタマブは皮膚下に注射されます。研究者の選択化学療法は静脈内投与されます。試験の詳細は以下の通りです:* 試験期間は最後の参加者が無作為化されてから最大5年となります。* すべての試験参加者は21日間のスクリーニング期間、治療期間、そして死亡まで続くフォローアップ期間があります。* 個々の参加者の推定試験期間は割り当てられた治療群によって異なります:* エプコリタマブを投与された参加者は28日間の治療サイクルとなります。エプコリタマブは最初の3か月間は週1回、その後6か月間は隔週、リンパ腫の進行や許容できない有害事象が現れるまで28日ごとに投与されます。* 研究者の選択(標準治療)化学療法を受けた参加者は、以下のいずれかの治療を受けます:* R-GemOx:1日目(または1日目 × 2日目)、および15日目(または15日目 / および16日目)に28日ごとに、最大4か月間投与;または * BR:1日目と2日目に3週間ごとに最大4.5か月間投与。本試験は、エコリタマブのオープンラベル、多施設、グローバルフェーズ3ランダム化試験です。このランダム化試験の目的は、再発し難治性のDLBCL(高用量化学療法および自家幹細胞移植(HDT-ASCT)に失敗または不適格な再発性のDLBCL(DLBCL)患者に対して、エコリタマブ(GEN3013、DuoBody-CD3xCD20®)の有効性を評価することです。治療段階では化学療法の変更は認められていません。米国および中国では全評価評価因子(OS)が主要評価項目であり、解析対象はすべてのランダム化参加者を対象としています。OS/無進行生存率(PFS)は、米国および中国を除く世界の他地域における二重主要評価項目であり、解析対象にもすべての参加者がランダム化されています。中国のGCT3013-05サブスタディはNCT07226752に登録されています。ステータス:ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING。フェーズ:フェーズ3。結果:公開済み。スポンサー:ゲンマブ。

candidates.abstract: This is a multicenter, open-label, Phase 1/2 study to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD) and clinical efficacy of DNL126 in participants with Sanfilippo syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA). In Part 1, the core study period is 25 weeks (approximately 6 months); followed by an open-label extension (OLE), which extends through Week 97 (approximately 18 months); and a long-term extension (LTE), which extends through Week 241 (Year 5). In Part 2, the core study period is 25 weeks in duration followed by an OLE, which extends through Week 49, and an LTE, which extends through Week 241 (Year 5). Participants with MPS IIIA will be enrolled in three planned cohorts, and additional participants with MPS IIIA may be enrolled in three optional cohorts. The study will enroll up to approximately 30 participants in total: 26 participants in Part 1 (Cohorts A1, A2, A3, B1, and B2 - not enrolling) and 4 participants in Part 2 (Cohort C1 - actively enrolling). Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE1, PHASE2. Sponsor: Denali Therapeutics Inc..

candidates.title: A Robust Protocol for Bio-Safety Re-Classification of Cell Lines Transduced with Lentiviral Vectors
candidates.abstract: Lentiviruses are a subfamily of RNA retroviruses that stably integrate their genetic information into host genomes. The transduction of cultured cells with safety-engineered replication-incompetent lentiviral vectors is a common procedure for delivering stable transgene overexpression in a wide variety of target lines and primary cell types. Work with lentiviral vectors and lentiviral vector-transduced cell cultures is generally managed under safety classification BL2/S2 due to risks from insertional mutagenesis. The prolonged culture of cells transduced with replication-incompetent lentiviral vectors under BL2/S2 conditions poses significant limitations to experimental downstream procedures and is not necessary once infectious lentiviral particles are no longer present. A safe transition of transduced cell lines to gene-technology safety level BL1/S1 requires certainty about the absence of any infectious particles to guarantee absence of risk for laboratory personnel. We have established a robust RT-PCR protocol to detect presence or absence of lentiviral vector mRNA components VSV-G, RRE, gag and pol, and for the detection of potential Psi-gag rearrangements. Our procedure detects lentiviral vector particles in cell culture supernatants using different MOIs for adherent and suspension cell lines, and we have characterized outcomes after defined serial washing steps and passaging procedures. We demonstrate that cell culture supernatants are free of detectable lentiviral vector particles after less than two passages. Our protocol establishes a robust and safe downgrading procedure for lentiviral vector transduced cells from BL2/S2 to BL1/S1 that can be easily adapted to any custom experimental setting.
candidates.title_ja: レンチバイラルベクターを用いた細胞株のバイオセーフティ再分類のための堅牢なプロトコル
candidates.abstract_ja: レンチウイルスは、遺伝情報を安定的に宿主ゲノムに統合するRNAレトロウイルスの亜科です。安全性が設計された複製不能力レンチウイルスベクターを用いた培養細胞のトランスデューションは、多様な標的系統や一次細胞タイプにおいて安定したトランスジェーン過剰発現を届ける一般的な手法です。レンチウイルスベクターおよびレンチウイルスベクターによる細胞培養の研究は、挿入変異誘発のリスクのため、一般的に安全性分類BL2/S2の下で管理されています。BL2/S2条件下で複製能力に欠けるレンチウイルスベクターによる細胞の長期培養は、実験的な下流手順に大きな制約をもたらし、感染性レンチウイルス粒子が存在しなくなった場合は不要となります。遺伝子技術安全性レベルBL1/S1への安全な移行には、感染性粒子の存在を確実に確認し、検査室職員のリスクなしを保証する必要があります。レンチウイルスベクターmRNA成分VSV-G、RRE、GAG、POLの有無を検出し、Psi-gagの再配置の可能性を検出するための堅牢なRT-PCRプロトコルを確立しました。我々の手法は、粘着細胞株と懸濁細胞株の異なるMOIを用いて細胞培養上清液中のレンチウイルスベクター粒子を検出し、定められた連続洗浄手順およびパッサージ手順後の結果を特徴付けています。細胞培養上清液は2回未満の通過後に検出可能なレンチウイルスベクター粒子が検出されないことを示しました。当プロトコルは、レンチウイルスベクターの細胞をBL2/S2からBL1/S1へと安全かつ厳格にダウングレードする手順を確立し、あらゆるカスタム実験環境に容易に適応できるものとなっています。

candidates.title: Phase 1/2 Dose Escalation and Cohort Expansion Study Evaluating MCLA-158 (Petosemtamab) as Single Agent or in Combination in Advanced Solid Tumors
candidates.abstract: This is a Phase 1/2 open-label, multi-center, multi-national study with an initial dose escalation part to determine the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of MCLA-158 single agent in patients with mCRC. The dose escalation part has been completed and the RP2D will be further evaluated in an expansion part of the study. Cohorts of selected solid tumor indications for which there is evidence of EGFR dependency and potential sensitivity to EGFR inhibition will be evaluated including head and neck cancer and metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). The study will further assess the safety, tolerability, PK, PD, immunogenicity, and anti-tumor activity of MCLA-158 in monotherapy or in combination with other therapies. Study Design: This open label, multicenter, first-in-human study consists of 2 parts. Part 1 is a dose escalation to find the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of MCLA-158 studying patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Enrollment in the dose escalation part has been completed. In the dose expansion (single-agent cohorts) part of the study, the activity, safety, and tolerability of MCLA-158 at 1500 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W) (preliminary RP2D) as a single agent will be evaluated in cohorts of selected solid tumor indications with dependency on EGFR signaling. The most recently enrolled cohorts were in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), gastric/ gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GEA) with EGFR amplification and/or high EGFR expression, esophageal carcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. In the dose expansion part of the study, safety was also characterized at two dose levels in (2L/3L) HNSCC. Enrollment is currently being explored in 2L/3L HNSCC and 3L/4L/5L mCRC (RAS/RAF wild type) patients. Additionally, in the dose expansion (combination cohorts) part of the study, the activity, safety, and tolerability of MCLA-158 at 1500 mg Q2W will be evaluated in combination with other therapies. Enrollment in the combination cohort of treatment of MCLA-158 with pembrolizumab for the treatment of patients with first line (1L) HNSCC is closed. Additionally, two combination cohorts of MCLA-158 with FOLFIRI or with FOLFOX chemotherapy (i.e., 5-fluorouracil \[5-FU\], leucovorin, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI) or oxaliplatin (FOLFOX)) will be explored in mCRC (RAS/RAF wild type) patients in the 1L/2L setting. Other expansion cohorts may be considered for monotherapy or combination treatment in the future Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE1, PHASE2. Sponsor: Genmab.

candidates.abstract_ja: 本試験は、mCRC患者におけるMCLA-158単剤の推奨第II相(RP2D)を決定するための初期用量増量部分を含む第1/2相オープンラベル、多施設、多国籍研究です。用量増強部分は完了しており、RP2Dは研究の拡大部分でさらに評価されます。EGFR依存性およびEGFR阻害に対する感受性の可能性が示される選択された固形腫瘍適応症のコホートを評価し、頭頸部がんおよび転移性大腸がん(mCRC)が含まれます。本研究では、単独療法または他の治療法との併用におけるMCLA-158の安全性、耐容性、PK、PD、免疫原性、抗腫瘍活性をさらに評価します。研究デザイン:このオープンラベル、多施設、初ヒト試験は2つの部分から構成されます。第1部は、転移性大腸がん(mCRC)患者を対象としたMCLA-158の推奨第II相用量(RP2D)を求めるための用量増量です。用量増量部分への登録は完了しています。用量拡大(単剤コホート)部分では、単剤として1500 mgを2週間ごとに(Q2W)(予備RP2D)として単剤としてMCLA-158を単剤として投与する活性、安全性、耐容性を、EGFRシグナル伝達に依存する選択された固形腫瘍適応症のコホートで評価します。最近登録されたコホートは、頭頸部扁平上皮癌(HNSCC)、EGFR増幅および/または高EGFR発現を伴う胃・胃食道接合部腺癌(GEA)、食道癌、肺扁平上皮癌の患者でした。投与拡大部分では、(2L/3L)HNSCCの2つの用量レベルで安全性も特徴づけられました。現在、2L/3L HNSCCおよび3L/4L/5L mCRC(RAS/RAF野生型)患者での登録が検討されています。さらに、投与拡大(組み合わせコホート)部分では、MCLA-158の活性、安全性、耐容性を他の治療法と併用して評価します。1ライン(1L)HNSCC患者を対象としたMCLA-158とペムブロリズマブの併用治療コホートへの登録は終了しています。さらに、MCLA-158とFOLFIRIまたはFOLFOX化学療法(すなわち5-フルオウラシル\[5-FU\]、ルコボリン、イリノテカン(FOLFIRI)またはオキサリプラチン(FOLFOX))を組み合わせた2つの複合コホートが、1L/2L環境でmCRC(RAS/RAF野生型)患者を対象に検討されます。将来的には単独治療または併用治療として検討される他の拡張コホートも検討される可能性があります。状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ1、フェーズ2。スポンサー:ジェンマブ。

candidates.abstract: This is a Phase 3 randomized, open-label study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of petosemtamab plus pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab in first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic PD-L1+ head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. This is a Phase 3 randomized, open-label study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of petosemtamab plus pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab in first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic PD-L1+ HNSCC. HNSCC patients should not have had previous systemic therapy administered in the incurable recurrent or metastatic setting, although previous systemic therapy as part of multimodal treatment for locally advanced disease is allowed if PD was ≥6 months after the last platinum-containing therapy dose. Previous treatments with anti PD-(L)1 or anti-EGFR therapies are not allowed. In the case of cetuximab, patients who have received cetuximab with radiotherapy as a local treatment and PD was \>1 year after the last dose of cetuximab are eligible. Status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Genmab.

candidates.title: Repurposing Antibody-Drug Conjugates for Theranostic Targeting of Nectin-4 and TROP2 in Bladder Cancer.
candidates.abstract: The application of antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapies in advanced bladder cancers may be improved through non-invasive molecular imaging and therapy with targeted radiation. Enfortumab and Sacituzumab, the antibody components for the ADCs PADCEV (Nectin-4 targeting) and TRODELVY (TROP2 targeting), were developed as ImmunoPET and radioimmunotherapeutic modalities in a HT1376 xenograft model of advanced bladder cancer. Both immuno-PET agents displayed distinct tumor uptake in vivo, with Sacituzumab showing higher accumulation (% ID/g) compared to Enfortumab, reflecting the higher TROP2 expression in this tumor model over Nectin-4. Further, both [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Enfortumab and [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Sacituzumab were effective in reducing the growth of tumors in vivo. The repurposing of well-validated ADC antibodies as theranostic radiopharmaceuticals is a promising approach for alternative or adjuvant therapies.
candidates.title_ja: 膀胱がんにおけるネクチン4およびTROP2のテラノスティック標的化のための抗体-薬物接合体の再利用。
candidates.abstract_ja: 進行性膀胱がんにおける抗体-薬物結合療法(ADC)の適用は、非侵襲的な分子画像診断および標的放射線治療によって改善される可能性があります。ADCであるPADCEV(ネクチン-4標的化)およびTRODELVY(TROP2ターゲット化)の抗体成分であるエンフォツマブおよびサチツズマブは、進行膀胱がんのHT1376異種移植モデルにおけるImmunoPETおよび放射免疫療法のモダリティとして開発されました。両免疫PET薬は生体内で腫瘍取り込みに異なる特徴を示し、サシツズマブはエンフォルツマブに比べて蓄積率(%ID/g)が高く、この腫瘍モデルではネクチン4よりも高いTROP2発現を示しました。さらに、[177Lu]Lu-DOTA-Enfortumabおよび[177Lu]Lu-DOTA-サシツズマブは、体内で腫瘍の増殖を抑制するのに効果的でした。十分に検証されたADC抗体を治療性放射性医薬品として再利用することは、代替療法や補助療法として有望なアプローチです。

candidates.title: A Phase 2a, Proof of Concept, Multicenter, Double Blind, Randomized, Placebo Controlled, Parallel Group Trial to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of ACT-777991 in Adults With Non-segmental Vitiligo
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this clinical trial is to learn how well ACT-777991 works, how safe it is and how well it is tolerated by adults with non-segmental vitiligo. The main question this clinical trial aims to answer is: • Can ACT-777991 help return color to the skin of the face of adults with non-segmental vitiligo? Researchers will compare ACT-777991 to placebo (a look-alike inactive treatment that contains no medicine) to see if ACT-777991 works to treat non-segmental vitiligo. Trial participants will: * Take the trial intervention (either ACT-777991 or placebo) daily for 24 weeks. * Visit the clinic 7 times for check-up and tests. The trial includes three trial periods: Following a Screening period, during which it will be checked if participants are eligible to take part, eligible participants will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive either ACT-777991 or placebo for 24 weeks (Trial intervention period). On completion of treatment, participants will be followed for 30 (+7) days (Follow-up period). Trial participation will end with a Follow-up visit (Participant Last Visit) at the end of the Follow-up period. The maximum trial duration for an individual participant is approximately 33 weeks including a screening period of up to 28 days, a treatment period of 24 weeks, and a follow-up period of up to 37 days. Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE2. Sponsor: Idorsia Pharmaceuticals Ltd..

candidates.title: 238 Off-the-shelf immune-shielded iPSC-derived armored CAR γδ T cells as a novel cell therapy to treat hepatocellular carcinoma
candidates.abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancerrelated mortality worldwide. Therapeutic options for advanced disease remain limited and show poor long-term outcomes. While chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies have transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, their success in solid tumors has been constrained by limited tumor infiltration, functional exhaustion, antigen heterogeneity, and - in the case of allogeneic products - allorejection. In vivo CAR T cell approaches may alleviate some manufacturing challenges but require validation of efficacy, safety, and therapeutic control.Methods To address these limitations, we developed allogeneic induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)derived CAR γδ T cells (CAR iγδ T cells) as a standardized, fully controllable ‘offtheshelf’ therapy for HCC. Our platform combines unlimited scalability and costeffective manufacturing with precise genome engineering at the iPSC stage. Targeted introduction of a γδ T cell receptor (TCR) and a proprietary HCCdirected CAR enable the generation of CAR iγδ T cells that inherently infiltrate solid tumors, do not induce graftversushost disease due to HLAindependent tumor recognition, and exhibit multimodal cytotoxicity. Additional immuneshielding modifications, a tumor microenvironment (TME) resistance edit, and an integrated safety switch prevent allorecognition, enhance persistence, and enable CAR iγδ T cell-specific therapeutic intervention if required.Results We established a scalable, xenofree differentiation process to generate highly pure iPSCderived CAR iγδ T cells without enrichment steps. The final immuneshielded armored CAR iγδ T cells displayed a predominantly naïve, nonexhausted phenotype and robust trimodal killing via NK receptors, the γδ TCR, and the CAR against an HCC cell line in vitro. Importantly, immune-shielding protected the cells from human NK cell- and T cellmediated killing and prevented cytokine release by these effector cells.Conclusions Collectively, our platform integrates precise genome engineering with scalable bioprocessing to deliver a GMPcompliant, broadly accessible, and costcompetitive CAR iγδ T cell therapy for HCC, combining trimodal cytotoxicity with immune shielding and TME resistance to address tumor escape, allorejection, and T cell exhaustion, and support durable tumor clearance.

candidates.title: Comparability of Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Canakinumab Administration With One Injection (200 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe or Auto-Injector Versus Two Injections (150 and 50 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe in Healthy Subjects.
candidates.abstract: This phase 1, randomized, open-label, single-dose, parallel-group study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetic (PK) comparability and safety of canakinumab administered as a single 200 mg subcutaneous injection via pre-filled syringes assembled within a needle safety device (PFS-NSD) by HCP and auto-injector (AI) by subject self-administration versus two injections of 150 + 50 mg via PFS-NSD by HCP. Healthy adults (18-55 years) were allocated to three arms: canakinumab 150 + 50 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 78), canakinumab 200 mg (AI; n = 76), and canakinumab 200 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 76). Multiplicity was addressed as two tests were compared with the same reference. Primary PK parameters were comparable across arms. The geometric mean ratios and 95% CI values of AUCinf, AUClast, and Cmax were within bioequivalence limits of 0.80-1.25 for both comparisons: (a) canakinumab 200 mg AI versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD and (b) canakinumab 200 mg PFS-NSD versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD. Median Tmax was comparable: 7, 9, and 7 days for canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD, 200 mg AI, and 200 mg PFS-NSD, respectively. Exploratory post-hoc analyses, assessing the impact of pause during the pandemic (N = 131 subjects recruited pre-pandemic) and evaluating partial AUC4weeks, suggested similar results. Canakinumab was well-tolerated, and no treatment-induced immunogenicity was observed.

candidates.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasonography of Orbital and Intraocular Pathologies in 24 Dogs and 6 Cats.
candidates.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) is a noninvasive and relatively safe imaging technique to assess ocular perfusion, showing high sensitivity and specificity for tumor characterization in human oncology, while reports on its application in canine and feline diseased eyes are limited. This study aimed to describe the CEUS features of orbital and intraocular pathologies in dogs and cats in order to evaluate its diagnostic value in detecting and characterizing various lesions. ANIMAL STUDIED: CEUS examinations of 30 animals (24 dogs, 6 cats) were evaluated retrospectively. PROCEDURES: Following B-mode ultrasonography, CEUS examinations utilizing sulfur hexafluoride were performed. Pathologies were categorized in one of the following groups: orbital neoplastic lesions, orbital inflammatory lesions, intraocular neoplastic lesions, intraocular inflammatory lesions and retinal detachment. Qualitative perfusion parameters, contrast intensity, enhancement pattern, perfusion type and time to wash-in and wash-out were evaluated. RESULTS: CEUS detected vascularization in orbital and intraocular pathologies, with variable enhancement characteristics. Persistent vascularization was observed in all cases of retinal detachment. In orbital and intraocular neoplastic lesions, CEUS improved lesion localization, assessment of interactions with surrounding tissues and tissue perfusion. For inflammatory pathologies such as abscesses, myositis, and steatitis, the additional diagnostic value of CEUS compared to B-mode ultrasonography was limited. CONCLUSION: Findings indicated that CEUS could identify a variety of orbital and intraocular pathologies and provided additional diagnostic information to B-mode ultrasonography, particularly for assessing neoplastic lesions and retinal detachments. CEUS has the potential to enhance ophthalmic ultrasonography in differentiating specific pathologies. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate its clinical use.

candidates.title: The Maternal Blood Transcriptome Reflects Molecular Signatures Associated With Large Offspring Syndrome and Other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Cattle.
candidates.abstract: Large offspring syndrome (LOS) in cattle is a phenomenon characterized by fetal overgrowth that is largely associated with calves derived from in vitro produced embryos. Here it was tested whether occurrence of LOS as well as two other adverse pregnancy outcomes, stillbirth and abortion, could be predicted using changes in the maternal blood transcriptome early in gestation. Blood samples were collected from Holstein and crossbred heifers at 40-50 days of gestation following embryo transfer of in vitro produced embryos. A total of 203 samples were selected for RNA-sequencing and used to compare recipients of embryos resulting in live-born calves of normal birth weight (control; n = 96) with recipients of embryos resulting in LOS calves (n = 15), stillbirths (n = 43), and abortion before 210 days of gestation (n = 49). Large offspring syndrome was defined based on birth weights greater than 2 standard deviations from the mean. The number of differentially-expressed genes (p < 0.01) was 32, 176, and 100 for comparisons of control versus LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. Biomarkers were identified in a randomly selected, balanced training dataset using Random Forest after filtering for differential expression. Markers were then tested in the held-out dataset through 6 machine learning models. The best biomarkers consisted of 26, 24, and 28 genes for LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. The accuracy of prediction ranged from 0.91 to 0.965 for LOS, 0.73 to 0.98 for stillbirth, and 0.62 to 0.96 for abortion. Despite the relatively small sample size, the model demonstrated high sensitivity for LOS classification, supporting that the maternal blood transcriptome in early pregnancy reflects molecular alterations associated with fetal overgrowth that can be predictive of the condition.
candidates.title_ja: 母体血液トランスクリプトームは、牛における大型子孫症候群やその他の妊娠不良に関連した分子シグネチャーを反映しています。
candidates.abstract_ja: 牛における大型子孫症候群(LOS)は、主にin vitro産卵由来の子牛に関連した胎児の過剰成長を特徴とする現象です。ここでは、LOSの発生および他の2つの有害な妊娠結果である死産と流産の発生を、妊娠初期の母体血液トランスクリプトームの変化を用いて予測できるかどうかを検証しました。体内で産生された胚の胚移植後、妊娠40〜50日のホルスタインおよび交配雌牛から血液サンプルを採取しました。合計203個のサンプルがRNAシーケンスのために選抜され、正常な出生体重の生児(対照群;n=96)を生じた胚の受因者と、LOS子牛(n=15)、死産(n=43)、妊娠210日前の中絶(n=49)を生じた胚の受領者(n=49)を比較しました。大型子孫症候群は、平均から2標準偏差を超える出生体重に基づいて定義されました。対照群とLOS、死産および中絶の比較では、差異発現遺伝子の数(p < 0.01)がそれぞれ32、176、100でした。バイオマーカーは、差異発現をフィルタリングした後、ランダムフォレストを用いたランダム選択のバランストレーニングデータセットで同定されました。マーカーは6つの機械学習モデルを通じて、ホールドアウトデータセットで検証されました。最良のバイオマーカーは、LOS、死産、中絶でそれぞれ26、24、28の遺伝子で構成されていました。予測精度はLOSで0.91から0.965、死産で0.73から0.98、中絶で0.62から0.96の範囲でした。比較的少ないサンプルサイズにもかかわらず、モデルはLOS分類に対する高い感度を示し、妊娠初期の母体血液トランスクリプトームが胎児の過剰増殖に関連する分子変化を反映し、この状態を予測できることを支持しました。

candidates.title: Quantifying the influence of contraction history on ex vivo bladder mechanics using optogenetics.
candidates.abstract: The micturition cycle involves passive expansion of the bladder as urine gradually accumulates, then active contraction during voiding. The high compliance of the bladder compared to other tissues is attributed to the interplay between smooth muscle cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) within the detrusor muscle. Current ex vivo methods to characterize bladder mechanics entail passive loading and unloading, which do not include the active contraction of the detrusor. The bladder does not return to the original configuration during these tests, leading to strain softening. We hypothesized that inducing controlled ex vivo detrusor contraction during the unloading phase of mechanical testing would improve the physiological relevance of the data by minimizing the strain softening that occurs during passive-only mechanical testing. We combined optogenetically mediated smooth muscle contraction with a custom mechanical testing platform to analyze the mechanical changes in bladder tissue compared to standard mechanical testing methods. Using a murine model expressing channelrhodopsin-2 in smooth muscle cells, we performed cyclical mechanical tests on bladder rings, both with and without optogenetic stimulation. Passive-only tests resulted in increased tissue compliance and strain softening. In contrast, induction of concentric contraction during unloading preserved the original tissue configuration. This method will enable future studies to link changes in ECM and cellular organization with bladder mechanics, leading to improved constitutive descriptions that drive computational analyses of in vivo behavior. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Traditional passive mechanical testing methods do not fully capture the dynamic nature of bladder mechanics. Our results demonstrate that incorporating active contraction into testing protocols provides a more physiologically relevant representation of bladder function and mechanical behavior. In addition, our results highlight the importance of choosing the proper reference configuration to define stretch when analyzing mechanical data. This work improves physiological relevance of ex vivo bladder mechanical data and has the potential to enhance the understanding of the mechanics of other active smooth muscle cell-containing tissues.
candidates.title_ja: オプトジェネティクスを用いた収縮履歴が体外膀胱力学に与える影響を定量化すること。
candidates.abstract_ja: 排便サイクルは尿が徐々に蓄積する際に膀胱が受動的に膨張し、排尿時に能動的に収縮する過程を含みます。膀胱の他の組織と比べて高いコンプライアンスは、平滑筋細胞とデトラソール筋内の細胞外マトリックス(ECM)との相互作用に起因しています。現在の膀胱力学を特徴づけるエクスビブ方法は受動的負荷と排出を伴い、デトラソールの能動的収縮は含まれません。これらの検査では膀胱は元の構成に戻らず、ストレスの軟化を引き起こします。機械的試験のアンロード段階で制御された体外デトラソール収縮を誘導することで、受動的のみ機械的試験中に発生するストレス軟化を最小限に抑え、データの生理的関連性を高めると仮説を立てました。光遺伝学的に媒介された平滑筋収縮とカスタム機械的検査プラットフォームを組み合わせ、標準的な機械的検査方法と比較して膀胱組織の機械的変化を分析しました。平滑筋細胞でチャネルロドプシン-2を発現するマウスモデルを用いて、光遺伝的刺激の有無を問わず膀胱リングに対して周期的機械的検査を行いました。受動的のみの検査では組織の遵守性が向上し、ストレスの軟化が促進されました。対照的に、アンロード時の同心円収縮誘導により元の組織構成が維持されました。この方法は、ECMや細胞組織の変化を膀胱力学と結びつける将来の研究を可能にし、生体内行動の計算解析を推進するより良い構成的記述につながるでしょう。意義の声明:従来の受動的機械的試験手法は、膀胱力学の動的性質を完全には捉えきれていません。我々の結果は、能動的収縮を試験プロトコルに組み込むことで、膀胱機能と機械的挙動をより生理学的に関連性のある表現で提供できることを示しています。さらに、機械的データを解析する際に伸縮を定義する適切な基準構成の選択の重要性も浮き彫りにします。この研究は、生体外膀胱力学データの生理学的関連性を高め、他の活動的平滑筋細胞を含む組織の力学理解を深める可能性を秘めています。

candidates.title: A Phase 1/2 Study of PRO1107 in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors
candidates.abstract: This is a global, open-label, multicenter Phase 1/2 study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and antitumor activity of GEN1107 (PRO1107) in participants with advanced solid tumors. This study consists of 2 parts, Part A: dose escalation and dose level expansion, and Part B: tumor specific expansion. This is a Phase 1/2 study of GEN1107, a protein tyrosine K 7 (PTK7) targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), to evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK, and antitumor activity of GEN1107 in participants with advanced solid tumors, including ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, triple negative breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, gastroesophageal cancer, and urothelial cancer. This study consists of 2 parts, Part A: Dose Escalation and Dose Level Expansion and Part B: Tumor Specific Expansion. In Part A, GEN1107 will be administered in different dosing regimens via intravenous (IV) infusion. Part B will be initiated at a dose level based on a comprehensive analysis of safety, tolerability, clinical PK, pharmacodynamics (PD) and activity data from Part A in up to 4 different tumor-specific cohorts of up to 40 participants per cohort. Participants will continue to receive study treatment until the first instance of disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision, consent withdrawal, study termination by the Sponsor, pregnancy, or death. Status: TERMINATED. Phase: PHASE1, PHASE2. Results: Posted. Sponsor: Genmab.
candidates.title_ja: 進行した固形腫瘍患者におけるPRO1107の第1/2相試験
candidates.abstract_ja: これは、進行した固形腫瘍の参加者におけるGEN1107(PRO1107)の安全性、耐容性、薬理動態(PK)、抗腫瘍活性を評価するための、グローバルなオープンラベル・多施設第1/2相試験です。本研究は2つの部分から構成されており、パートA:用量増加および投与レベル拡大、パートB:腫瘍特異的拡大です。これは、GEN1107、タンパク質チロシンK7(PTK7)標的抗体薬剤結合体(ADC)の第1/2相試験で、進行した固形腫瘍(卵巣がん、子宮内膜がん、トリプルネガム性乳がん、非小細胞肺がん、胃食道がん、尿路上皮がんを含む)のGEN1107の安全性、耐容性、PK、抗腫瘍活性を評価することを目的としています。本研究は2つのパートA:用量増量および用量レベル拡大、B部分:腫瘍特異的拡大の2部構成です。パートAでは、GEN1107を異なる投与方式で静脈内(IV)輸液で投与します。パートBは、最大40名の参加者が1コホートあたり最大40名の異なる腫瘍特異的コホートにおいて、安全性、耐容性、臨床PK、薬理動態(PD)、活性データの包括的な解析に基づく用量レベルで開始されます。参加者は、疾患進行、許容できない毒性、研究者の決定、同意撤回、スポンサーによる研究終了、妊娠、または死亡が初めて発生するまで、引き続き研究治療を受けます。状態:終了。フェーズ:フェーズ1、フェーズ2。結果:公開済み。スポンサー:ジェンマブ。

candidates.title: A Phase II, Randomized, Open-label Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics (PK) of Maintenance Cabozantinib (XL184) Plus Best Supportive Care (BSC) Versus BSC in Children, Adolescents and Young Adults (AYA) With Unresectable Residual Osteosarcoma Either at Diagnosis or at First Relapse After Standard Treatment
candidates.abstract: The participants of this study will be children, adolescents, and young adults with residual osteosarcoma, which cannot be removed completely through surgery. Participants will have achieved a partial response or stable disease at the end of conventional chemotherapy. Osteosarcoma is cancer of the bone. The cancer cells make immature bone cells, known as osteoid. Osteosarcoma is very rare, but it is the most common type of bone cancer in children and teens. It is most common in teens and young adults. In this study, participants will receive either cabozantinib and best supportive care or the best supportive care alone. Best supportive care will be provided at the investigator's discretion and according to institutional guidelines. It includes antibiotics, nutritional support, correction of metabolic disorders, optimal symptom control and pain management (including radiotherapy), etc. but does not include tumor specific therapy. Cabozantinib will be taken by mouth (orally), as a tablet, once a day. Cabozantinib will be provided to participants who tolerate it for as long as their disease does not progress. Participants in the study receiving best supportive care alone may switch to treatment with cabozantinib and best supportive care if their disease progresses and if other eligibility criteria are met. Participants may withdraw consent to participate at any time. The estimated duration of the study for participants is 24 months, however a participant could remain in the study longer if demonstrating treatment benefit. Status: TERMINATED. Phase: PHASE2. Results: Posted. Sponsor: Ipsen.
fields: Osteosarcoma in Adolescents and Young Adults

candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究の参加者は、手術で完全に除去できない残存骨肉腫を持つ子ども、青年、若年成人です。参加者は従来の化学療法終了時に部分的回復または安定した病況を達成しています。変形肉腫は骨のがんです。がん細胞は未熟な骨細胞(骨組織)を形成します。変形肉腫は非常に稀ですが、子供やティーンエイジャーで最も一般的な骨がんのタイプです。特に10代および若年成人に多く見られます。本研究では、参加者はカボザンチニブと最良支持療法、または単独で最良の支持療法を受けます。最良の支持療法は研究者の裁量と機関ガイドラインに従って提供されます。抗生物質、栄養サポート、代謝障害の矯正、最適な症状管理および疼痛管理(放射線治療を含む)などが含まれますが、腫瘍特異的治療は含まれません。カボザンチニブは経口(経口)で1日1回錠剤として服用されます。カボザンチニブは、病気が進行しない限り耐性がある参加者に提供されます。最良支持療法のみを受けている参加者は、病気が進行し他の適格基準を満たした場合、カボザンチニブおよび最良支持療法の治療に切り替えることができます。参加者はいつでも参加同意を撤回することができます。参加者の研究期間は推定24か月ですが、治療効果が示された場合はより長く研究に留まる可能性があります。状態:終了。フェーズ:フェーズ2。結果:公開済み。スポンサー:イプセン。

candidates.title: An Interventional Phase 3, Open-label, Two-cohort Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Fosmanogepix in Adult Patients With Invasive Mold Infections Caused by Aspergillus Spp., Fusarium Spp., Lomentospora Prolificans, Mucorales Fungi, or Other Multidrug Resistant Molds
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of fosmanogepix (administered IV or oral) for the treatment of adult patients with invasive mold infections. The study is looking for patients who have been diagnosed with invasive mold infections. The maximum study duration will be approximately 8 months, including a target study treatment duration of 84 days which can be extended up to 180 days and follow-up period. The patient will be assigned to one of two treatment cohorts: Cohort A (primary therapy): Patients will receive either the study drug or institutional standard of care antifungal treatment. Cohort B (salvage treatment; i.e. treatment given after patients did not respond to previous treatments or did not tolerate them): Patients will receive the study drug The primary aim is to compare the all cause mortality with a fixed threshold at Day 42. Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: Basilea Pharmaceutica.

candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究の目的は、浸潤性カビ感染の成人患者の治療におけるフォスマノゲピックス(静脈注射または経口投与)の有効性と安全性を評価することです。本研究は侵襲性カビ感染と診断された患者を探しています。最大研究期間は約8か月で、対象治療期間は84日で最大180日まで延長可能で、追跡期間も設けられます。患者は2つの治療コホートのいずれかに割り当てられます:コホートA(主治療法):患者は研究薬剤または施設標準治療の抗真菌治療を受けます。コホートB(サルベージ治療;すなわち、患者が以前の治療に反応しなかったか耐性がなかった後に投与される治療):患者は研究薬を投与します。主な目的は、42日目に固定された閾値と全死亡率を比較することです。状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ3。スポンサー:Basilea Pharmaceutica。

candidates.title: A Phase II, Multi-site, Open-label Trial Evaluating the Safety and Efficacy of Pumitamig and Bevacizumab as Monotherapy and Pumitamig in Combination With Temozolomide in Patients With Recurrent Glioblastoma
candidates.abstract: This multi-site Phase II study will enroll adults with histologically confirmed diagnosis of World Health Organization (WHO) Grade IV glioblastoma (GBM), isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype consistent with WHO central nervous system (CNS) 2021 criteria who have received prior first-line treatment including with at least radiotherapy and temozolomide, with a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) ≥60, adequate organ function, and at least one measurable lesion according to the response assessment in neuro-oncology (RANO) 2.0 criteria. Participants will be randomized to the two treatment Arms 1 and 2. After sponsor evaluation of the initial safety signals from Arm 1, it will be determined whether to initiate Arm 3. Participants who have disease progression in Arm 2 may be eligible to receive pumitamig. There will be a screening period of up to 28 days, followed by a treatment period lasting up to 2 years. Participants will be followed-up for safety for up to 90 days after the last dose of study treatment or until the participant initiates new anticancer treatment (e.g., systemic, radiotherapy/surgery). Thereafter, survival follow-up will be conducted until the participant dies, the participant withdraws consent for survival status follow-up, loss of contact, or study termination (whichever occurs first). Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE2. Sponsor: BioNTech SE.

candidates.abstract_ja: この多施設第II相試験は、世界保健機関(WHO)グレードIV膠芽腫、イソシトレート脱水素酵素(IDH)ワイルド型でWHO中枢神経系(CNS)2021基準に適合し、放射線療法およびテモゾロミドを含む事前の第一選択治療を受け、カルノフスキーパフォーマンスステータス(KPS)≥60、適切な臓器機能、神経腫瘍学の反応評価(RANO 2.0)基準に基づく少なくとも1つの測定可能な病変を組織学的に確定した成人を登録します。参加者は2つの治療群1および2に無作為に割り当てられます。群1の初期安全性シグナルのスポンサー評価後、群3を開始するかどうかが決定されます。群2で進行が見られる参加者はプミタミグの投与資格がある可能性があります。スクリーニング期間は最大28日間、その後治療期間は最大2年間続きます。参加者は、最終投与後最大90日間、または新たな抗がん治療(例:全身療法、放射線療法/手術)を開始するまで安全性の確認を続けます。その後は、参加者が死亡するか、生存状況のフォローアップ、連絡喪失、または研究終了(いずれか早い方)への同意撤回まで生存追跡が行われます。状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ2。スポンサー:BioNTech SE。

candidates.title: A Phase I Study to Evaluate the Safety and Dosimetry of Imaging With 68Ga-OncoACP3 in Prostate Cancer
candidates.abstract: The aim of this study is to assess the safety and dosimetry of imaging with \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 in patients with prostate cancer. This is a phase I, non-randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical trial to evaluate primary the safety and dosimetry of a single dose of \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 and, secondly, its uptake, biodistribution, PK and excretion. The Acid Phosphatase 3 (ACP3) is expressed in primary and metastatic prostate cancer lesions. OncoACP3 is a new ligand for ACP3: its radiolabelled version can be used as a PET radiotracer for the diagnostic imaging of prostate cancer. In this trial, 68Ga-OncoACP3 is offered to prostate cancer patients who already received standard of care imaging and might therefore complement available modalities. Eligible patients for this trial are prostate cancer patients, aged 18 years or more with: * suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy * suspected recurrence based on elevated serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level (i.e., a progressive and confirmed serum PSA level \> 0.2 ng/mL) * metastatic disease who might be candidates for treatment with 177Lu-labelled PSMA ligands. All patients will undergo PET/CT imaging with \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3. Patients are divided into two cohorts: * Cohort A: 5 male patients without visceral or bone metastases, which would interfere with dosimetry evaluation of healthy organs. * Cohort B: all patients who meet the eligibility criteria (up to 15 patients) Both cohorts are recruited in parallel, and patients are assigned to the respective cohort based on their disease extent. Whenever possible, patients are enrolled in cohort A, unless they are unsuitable for cohort A, or the required number of patients has already been enrolled in cohort A. All patients will receive a single intravenous bolus administration of 250 MBq (150 - 275 MBq) \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 and biodistribution, PK, excretion, and dosimetry of \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 will be assessed based on a series of PET/CT scans, blood and urine sampling. Full dosimetry evaluations will be performed for all patients in cohort A. Dosimetry in the other patients may be performed to the extent that it is possible based on their disease burden (i.e., only organs not affected by malignant lesions can be evaluated), as appropriate. All patients will be assessed for safety. In addition, relative uptake to appropriate reference tissue of \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 as well as semiquantitative parameters such as SUVmax/SUVmean/SUVsd, are determined. The correlation of \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 uptake with immunopathology staining for ACP3 will be evaluated in patients undergoing surgery or tumor biopsy collection. For patients who undergo PSMA-PET/CT within 6 weeks before or after the \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3-PET/CT scan, the lesion detection rate will be compared. Full dosimetry evaluations will be performed for all patients in cohort A. Dosimetry in the other patients may be performed to the extent that it is possible based on their disease burden (i.e., only organs not affected by malignant lesions can be evaluated), as appropriate. Status: COMPLETED. Phase: PHASE1. Sponsor: Philogen S.p.A..
candidates.title_ja: 前立腺がんにおける68Ga-OncoACP3の画像診断の安全性と線量評価を目的とした第I相試験
candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究の目的は、前立腺がん患者における \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 の画像診断の安全性と線量評価です。これは第I相、非ランダム化、オープンラベル、多施設臨床試験で、単回量の \[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3 の安全性と線量を一次的に評価し、次にその取り込み、生体分布、PK、排泄を評価します。酸リン酸3(ACP3)は原発性および転移性前立腺がん病変に発現します。OncoACP3 はACP3の新しいリガンドであり、その放射性標識版は前立腺がんの診断画像におけるPET放射性トレーサーとして使用できます。本試験では、68Ga-OncoACP3 が既に標準治療画像診断を受けている前立腺がん患者に提供され、利用可能なモダリティを補完する可能性があります。本試験の対象患者は、18歳以上の前立腺がん患者で、以下の条件を満たします:* 初期決定的治療の候補である転移の疑いがある * 血清前立腺特異的抗原(PSA)レベル(すなわち進行性かつ確定した血清PSAレベル \>0.2 ng/mL)に基づく再発の疑い * 177Lu標識PSMAリガンドによる治療候補となる可能性のある転移性疾患。すべての患者は、[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3を用いたPET/CT画像検査を受けます。患者は2つのコホートに分けられます: * コホートA:内臓または骨転移のない男性患者5名で、健康な臓器の線量評価に支障が出る。* コホートB:適格基準を満たす全患者(最大15名)両コホートは並行して募集され、患者は疾患の程度に応じてそれぞれのコホートに割り当てられます。可能な限り、患者はコホートAに登録されますが、対象外、または必要な患者数がすでにコホートAに登録されている場合を除きます。すべての患者は、250 MBq(150 - 275 MBq)の静脈内ボーラス投与を単回受けます。GA-OncoACP3は、PET/CTスキャン、血液および尿の一連の検査に基づいて、生体分布、PK、排泄量、投与量を評価します。コホートAのすべての患者に対して完全な線量測定が行われます。その他の患者については、その疾患負荷(すなわち悪性病変の影響を受けていない臓器のみ評価可能)に応じて投与されることがあります。すべての患者は安全性のため評価されます。さらに、適切な参照組織への相対的な取り込み量や、SUVmax/SUV平均/SUVsdなどの半定量的パラメータも測定します。手術または腫瘍生検採取を受ける患者において、[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3の取り込みとACP3の免疫病理染色の相関関係が評価されます。[68Ga\]Ga-OncoACP3-PET/CTスキャンの前後6週間以内にPSMA-PET/CTを受けた患者については、病変検出率を比較します。コホートAのすべての患者に対して完全な線量測定が行われます。その他の患者の線量測定は、疾患負荷に応じて可能な限り実施されることがあります(すなわち悪性病変の影響を受けていない臓器のみ評価可能)。状態:完了。フェーズ:フェーズ1。スポンサー:フィロジェンS.p.A.

candidates.title: An Open-Label, Multicenter, First-in-Human Trial of GEN3018 in Participants With Relapsed or Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia or Higher-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndrome
candidates.abstract: The drug that will be investigated in the trial is an antibody, GEN3018. Since this is the first trial of GEN3018 in humans, the main purpose is to evaluate safety. In addition to safety, the trial will determine the recommended GEN3018 dose(s) to be tested in a larger group of participants and assess preliminary anti-tumor activity of GEN3018. GEN3018 will be studied in refractory (resistant to treatment) or relapsed (disease has returned) acute myeloid leukemia (also known as R/R AML) and refractory or relapsed higher-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (also known as R/R HR-MDS). The trial consists of 2 parts: Part 1 Dose Escalation will test increasing doses of GEN3018 to identify a safe dose level to be tested in the next part Part 2 Dose Refinement will further test the GEN3018 dose(s) determined from the Dose Escalation. Up to 78 participants may be treated in this trial (up to 60 participants in Part 1; up to 18 participants in Part 2). For an individual participant in the trial, the estimated treatment duration will be up to 1 year. Participation in the trial will require regular scheduled visits to the site. At site visits, there will be various tests (such as blood draws) to monitor whether the treatment is safe and effective. Participants will also be contacted every 3 months after treatment ends to monitor how they are doing. All participants in the trial will receive active drug (ie, GEN3018); no one will be given placebo. This is a FIH, Phase 1, open-label, multicenter trial in participants with R/R AML or R/R HR-MDS, to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), immunogenicity, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity of GEN3018. The trial will be conducted in 2 parts: Dose Escalation (Part 1) and Dose Refinement (Part 2). Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE1. Sponsor: Genmab.

candidates.abstract_ja: 試験で調査される薬剤は抗体ですGEN3018。これはヒトにおけるGEN3018の初試験であるため、主な目的は安全性の評価です。安全性に加え、試験ではより大きな参加者群で試験される推奨GEN3018用量を決定し、GEN3018の初期の抗腫瘍活性を評価します。GEN3018難治性(治療抵抗性)または再発性(疾患再発)の急性骨髄性白血病(R/R AMLとも呼ばれる)および難治性または再発性高リスク骨髄異形成症候群(R/R HR-MDS)で研究されます。試験は2つの部分から構成されます。第1部:用量増量でGEN3018の用量を増やし、次の第1部で安全な用量レベルを特定します。第2部では用量調整で、用量増量から決定されたGEN3018用量をさらに検証します。この試験では最大78名の参加者が治療を受けられます(第1部は最大60名、第2部は最大18名)。試験の個別参加者の推定治療期間は最大1年となります。試験への参加には定期的な会場訪問が必要です。現地訪問では、治療の安全性と有効性を監視するための採血などの検査が行われます。治療終了後、参加者には3か月ごとに連絡があり、経過状況を監視します。試験の全参加者には有効薬(すなわちGEN3018)が投与されます。プラセボは投与されません。これはFIH、第1相オープンラベル、多施設試験で、R/R AMLまたはR/R HR-MDSの参加者を対象に、GEN3018の安全性、耐容性、薬理動態(PK)、免疫原性、薬理動態、および初期の抗腫瘍活性を評価することを目的としています。試験は2つのパートで実施されます:用量増強(パート1)と用量精錬(パート2)。ステータス:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ1。スポンサー:ジェンマブ。

candidates.abstract: The study will assess how ARGX-121 affects immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) disease outcomes, such as renal function, how it is distributed and eliminated from the body, and how the immune system responds in adults with IgAN. candidates.title: An Open-Label Extension to Investigate the Long-Term Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of DNL310 in Patients With Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II (MPS II) From Study DNLI-E-0002 or Study DNLI-E-0007
candidates.abstract: This is a multiregional open-label extension (OLE) to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of long-term treatment with tividenofusp alfa (DNL310), an investigational central nervous system (CNS)-penetrant intravenous (IV) enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for Hunter syndrome (MPS II). Participants who complete at least through the Week 49 visit in Study DNLI-E-0002 and do not discontinue study intervention early and participants who complete Study DNLI-E-0007 will be enrolled in this OLE. All participants will receive DNL310 for up to 5 years from the time of entry in this OLE. Participants, site staff, and the Sponsor will remain blinded to the original treatment assignment for participants entering this OLE from Study DNLI-E-0007. Status: ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION. Phase: PHASE2, PHASE3. Sponsor: Denali Therapeutics Inc..

candidates.title: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Masked, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Efgartigimod PH20 SC PFS in Adult Participants With Graves' Disease Inadequately Controlled With Antithyroid Drugs
candidates.abstract: The main purpose of this study is to look at how efgartigimod affects thyroid function in adults with Graves' Disease (GD). The study will also check whether efgartigimod is safe and well tolerated. It will look at how efgartigimod is distributed and eliminated in the body, how it changes antibody levels, and how the immune system responds to it. The study consists of a part A double-blinded treatment period, a part B treatment/observation period and a part C open-label treatment/observation period. During the part A and part B treatment periods, participants will receive efgartigimod PH20 SC via Prefilled Syringe (PFS) or placebo. During the part C open-label treatment period, participants will receive efgartigimod PH20 SC PFS. Participation in the different parts of the study will depend on the participant's response to treatment. The total study duration for participants ranges from 63 to 135 weeks, depending on the response to treatment. More information can be found here: https://clinicaltrials.argenx.com/vitalithy Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE3. Sponsor: argenx.

candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究の主な目的は、エフガルティジモドが成人のバセドウ病(GD)における甲状腺機能にどのように影響するかを調べることです。また、エフガルチジモドが安全かつ耐容性が高いかどうかも確認します。エフガルチジモドが体内でどのように分布・除去されるか、抗体レベルの変化、免疫系の反応についても調べます。本研究は、パートAの二重盲検治療期間、パートBの治療・観察期間、パートCのオープンラベル治療・観察期間で構成されています。パートAおよびパートBの治療期間中、参加者はプレフィルドシリンジ(PFS)またはプラセボを通じてエフガルティジモドPH20 SCを投与します。パートCのオープンラベル治療期間中は、参加者はエフガルティジモドPH20 SC PFSを受け取ります。研究の各部分への参加は、参加者の治療反応によって異なります。参加者の総研究期間は、治療への反応に応じて63週間から135週間の範囲です。詳細はこちらをご覧ください:https://clinicaltrials.argenx.com/vitalithy 状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ3。スポンサー:argenx。

candidates.title: A Master Protocol for an Exploratory, Phase 2a, Proof-of-Concept Platform Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Multiple Regimens in Participants With Myasthenia Gravis
candidates.abstract: ADAPT Forward is a platform study with the aim to look at how safe different drugs are and how well they work for people with myasthenia gravis. The goal is to find the best therapeutic approach to reduce patients' side effects and improve their quality of life. This is a platform study and is governed by a single master protocol that enables multiple regimens to be evaluated in separate intervention-specific appendixes (ISAs). The key design structure of the platform study comprises: common master protocol screening period, ISA-specific screening period, ISA treatment period of variable duration and design and ISA safety follow-up/follow-up period of variable duration. Details on each study period will be specified in the ISAs. Following ISAs are included in this platform study: * NCT07284420 - ADAPT Forward 1 - a study to evaluate empasiprubart IV as add-on therapy to efgartigimod IV in participants with AChR-Ab seropositive generalized myasthenia gravis with a partial clinical response to efgartigimod (https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07284420) * NCT07673627 - Adapt Forward 2 - a Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of Empasiprubart IV Monotherapy in Participants With AChR-Ab Seropositive Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07673627) More information can be found here: https://clinicaltrials.argenx.com/adaptforward Status: RECRUITING. Sponsor: argenx.

candidates.abstract_ja: ADAPT Forwardは、重症筋無力症患者に対する異なる薬剤の安全性や効果を調べることを目的としています。目的は、患者の副作用を減らし、生活の質を向上させる最適な治療アプローチを見つけることです。これはプラットフォーム研究であり、複数のレジメンを個別の介入特異的虫垂(ISA)で評価できる単一のマスタープロトコルによって運営されています。プラットフォーム研究の主要な設計構造は、共通マスタープロトコルスクリーニング期間、ISA特異スクリーニング期間、可変期間およびデザインのISA治療期間、および可変期間のISA安全性追跡期間/追跡期間で構成されています。各研究期間の詳細はISAsで明記されます。以下のISAがこのプラットフォーム研究に含まれています:* NCT07284420 - ADAPT Forward 1 - AChR-Ab陽性全般性重症筋無力症患者におけるempasiprubart IVをエフガルティジモドIVの補助療法として評価する研究(https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07284420) * NCT07673627 - Adapt Forward 2 - AChR-Ab陽性全般性重症筋無力症(https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07673627)患者におけるEmpasiprubart IV単剤療法の安全性、耐容性および有効性を評価する研究 詳細はこちらをご覧ください:https://clinicaltrials.argenx.com/adaptforward ステータス:募集中。スポンサー:argenx。

candidates.abstract: The purpose of this study is to characterize and assess the evolution of hearing impairment of patients with adulthood-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss carrying mutations on GJB2 gene. This study aims to characterize patients with adulthood-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss not due to any underlying medical condition (likely due to a genetic cause) and to assess the evolution of hearing impairment of those carrying mutations in GJB2 gene. Patients who present with adulthood-onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss will be screened for the presence of mutation involved in hearing impairment. Patients with GJB2 mutations will be proposed to continue in a follow-up period. Status: TERMINATED. Sponsor: Sensorion.

candidates.title: A Phase I Study to Evaluate the Safety and Preliminary Signs of Efficacy of [177Lu]Lu-OncoFAP-23 Alone or in Combination With L19-IL2 as a Treatment of Metastatic FAP-positive Solid Tumors
candidates.abstract: The aim of this study is to assess the safety of \[177Lu\]Lu-OncoFAP-23 alone or in combination with L19-IL2 for the treatment of advanced/metastatic Fibroblast Activation Protein (FAP)-positive solid tumors and to establish a Recommended Dose (RD). This study is a prospective phase I, open-label, multiple ascending, multi-center dose escalation study to evaluate the safety and preliminary signs of efficacy of \[177Lu\]Lu-OncoFAP-23 alone and in combination with the antibody-cytokine conjugate L19-IL2 for the treatment of advanced/metastatic FAP-positive solid tumors. Eligible patients for this trial are male or non-pregnant and non-breastfeeding females aged 18 years or more, able to give informed consent. Up to 56 evaluable patients will be enrolled in the trial and the trial is divided into two parts: 1. Part I - Dose escalation part (2-36 pts) This dose escalation part of the study is designed as a standard 3+3 escalation scheme. Not more than 2 patients per cohort are treated simultaneously during the Dose Limiting Toxicity (DLT) observation period from Day 1 to Day 28 of the first cycle. Patients per cohort will be assigned to different dose levels of the study drug. 2. Part II - Dose expansion part (20 pts) After completion of the dose escalation part, additional 20 patients will be enrolled at the RD to better understand the safety profile and to explore early signs of efficacy in different disease indications. Patients will be randomly assigned to arm 1 (monotherapy) or arm 2 (combination therapy) (10 patients each). Both in part I and II, patients can receive up to 4 consecutive cycles of radioligand therapy every 8 (± 1) weeks. The primary objective of this study is to assess the safety of \[177Lu\]Lu-OncoFAP-23 alone or in combination with L19-IL2 for the treatment of advanced/metastatic FAP-positive malignancies and to establish a Recommended Dose (RD). Secondary objectives include evaluation of pharmacokinetics and the collection of initial signs of efficacy of the treatment. Status: RECRUITING. Phase: PHASE1. Sponsor: Philogen S.p.A..
candidates.title_ja: 転移性FAP陽性固形腫瘍治療として、[177Lu]Lu-OncoFAP-23単独またはL19-IL2と併用して使用した場合の安全性および有効性の予備的兆候を評価する第I相試験
candidates.abstract_ja: 本研究の目的は、進行性/転移性線維芽細胞活性化タンパク質(FAP)陽性固形腫瘍の治療において、\[177Lu\]]Lu-OncoFAP-23単独またはL19-IL2と併用して安全性を評価し、推奨用量(RD)を確立することです。本研究は、進行性/転移性FAP陽性固形腫瘍治療において、Lu-OncoFAP-23単独および抗体サイトカイン結合L19-IL2と併用して安全性および有効性の予備的兆候を評価する前向きI相オープンラベル、複数増加型、多施設投与試験です。本試験の対象患者は、18歳以上、かつインフォームドコンセントが可能な男性または妊娠中でない非授乳女性です。最大56名の評価可能な患者が試験に登録され、試験は2つの部分に分かれます。1. パートI - 用量増量部分(2〜36ポイント) この用量増量部分は標準的な3+3増量スキームとして設計されています。第1サイクルの1日目から28日目までの用量制限毒性(DLT)観察期間中、1コホートあたり最大2名の患者が同時に治療されます。各コホートの患者は異なる用量レベルの薬剤に割り当てられます。2. パートII - 用量拡大パート(20ポイント) 用量増量部分終了後、追加の20名の患者がRDに登録され、安全性プロファイルの理解と異なる疾患適応症における有効性の早期兆候を探ります。患者は群1(単独療法)または群2(併用療法)(それぞれ10名)にランダムに割り当てられます。パートIおよびIIの両方で、患者は最大4サイクル連続で8週間(±1)周期に放射線リガンド療法を受けることができます。本研究の主な目的は、進行性または転移性FAP陽性悪性腫瘍の治療におけるL19-IL2単独またはL19-IL2併用の安全性評価および推奨用量(RD)の確立です。副次的な目的には薬剤動態の評価および治療の初期有効性兆候の収集が含まれます。状況:募集中。フェーズ:フェーズ1。スポンサー:Philogen S.p.A.

candidates.title: Bovine serum Albumin-Mediated effects on colonic Solubility, mucus Permeation, and absorption of celecoxib.
candidates.abstract: Celecoxib was used as a model compound in fasted state simulated colonic fluid (FaSSCoF) to investigate equilibrium drug solubility (Seq), protein binding using rapid equilibrium dialysis (RED), flux and permeability (Papp) across porcine colonic mucus (PCM), and in vivo colonic absorption using a rat intracolonic instillation model. The primary focus was on the role of bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a solubilizing and binding constituent, while bile salts (sodium taurodeoxycholate, TDC) with lecithin and poloxamer 407 were included as comparative systems to evaluate how differences in solubilizer type influence celecoxib permeability and absorption. BSA demonstrated a pronounced solubilizing effect on celecoxib with a 1:1 M binding ratio, increasing the apparent Seq from 5.1 µg/mL to 92 µg/mL in FaSSCoF containing 15 mg/mL BSA. Under these conditions, diffusion across PCM increased approximately seven-fold compared with FaSSCoF without BSA, accompanied by a four-fold increase in colonic absorption in vivo. In contrast, when celecoxib concentration was maintained constant and BSA was subsequently added to FaSSCoF, diffusion across PCM decreased up to ten-fold at BSA concentrations of 1.5 mg/mL, accompanied by an approximately 30 % decrease in colonic absorption in vivo. This behavior is consistent with an increased BSA-bound fraction and a reduced free drug concentration available for transport. The addition of TDC with lecithin or poloxamer 407 similarly increased celecoxib diffusion across PCM and colonic absorption when celecoxib was dissolved at Seq in FaSSCoF, although no statistically significant differences were observed between the solubilizing systems. Overall, these findings demonstrate that solubilizing constituents in colonic fluids can substantially increase drug solubility, mucus permeation, and colonic absorption, highlighting the importance of accounting for protein-drug interactions when evaluating drug behavior in the colon.
candidates.title_ja: 牛血清 アルブミン媒介による大腸溶解度、粘液浸透、セレコキシブの吸収への影響。
candidates.abstract_ja: セレコキシブは、空腹時の模擬大腸液(FaSSCoF)におけるモデル化合物として、平衡薬物溶解度(Seq)、急速平衡透析(RED)によるタンパク質結合、豚の大腸粘液(PCM)におけるフラックスおよび透過性(Papp)、およびラットの腸内注入モデルを用いた生体内大腸吸収の調査に用いられました。主な焦点は、溶解性および結合成分としての牛血清アルブミン(BSA)の役割であり、胆汁塩(タウロデオキシコレート、TDC)とレシチンおよびポロキサーマー407を比較系として含め、溶解剤タイプの違いがセレコキシブの透過性と吸収にどのように影響するかを評価しました。BSAはセレコキシブに対して1:1 M結合比で顕著な溶解効果を示し、15 mg/mL BSAを含むFaSSCoFにおいて見かけのSeqが5.1 μg/mLから92 μg/mLに増加しました。これらの条件下では、PCMを介した拡散はBSAなしのFaSSCoFと比べて約7倍増加し、体内での大腸吸収も4倍増加しました。対照的に、セレコキシブ濃度を一定に保ち、その後にBSAをFaSSCoFに加えた場合、1.5 mg/mLのBSA濃度でPCMを越えた拡散は最大10倍に減少し、生体内での大腸吸収は約30%減少しました。この挙動は、BSA結合割合の増加と輸送可能な自由薬物濃度の減少と一致しています。TDCをレシチンまたはポロキサーム407と併用すると、セレコキシブをSeqでFaSSCoFに溶解した際のPCMでの拡散と大腸吸収が同様に増加しましたが、溶解系間で統計的に有意な差は認められませんでした。総じて、これらの発見は大腸液中の溶解性成分が薬物溶解度、粘液透過率、大腸吸収を大幅に増加させることを示し、大腸内の薬物挙動を評価する際にタンパク質間相互作用を考慮する重要性を強調しています。

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Epcoritamab Monotherapy and in Combination With Lenalidomide as First-line Therapy for Anthracycline-ineligible Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Patients, an Open-label, Randomized, Multicenter, Global Phase 2 Trial
candidates.abstract: The purpose of the study is to examine efficacy and safety of epcoritamab with and without lenalidomide in newly diagnosed elderly patients with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) who cannot tolerate anthracycline therapy. Epcoritamab (also known as EPKINLY™, GEN3013 and DuoBody®-CD3xCD20) is an antibody that has already been tested in several clinical studies. All patients will receive active treatment. There is an equal chance of receiving epcoritamab or epcoritamab plus lenalidomide. This is an open-label, multicenter, global phase-2 trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of epcoritamab monotherapy and epcoritamab plus lenalidomide in elderly patients who are deemed anthracycline ineligible. The trial is designed in two stages: * Stage 1 which includes a safety run-in phase in each arm * Stage 2, an expansion of the selected treatment from Stage 1 Status: TERMINATED. Phase: PHASE2. Sponsor: Genmab.
